appearance.twig.note: Sargent's Manual (2nd ed. 1922, read at the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18), as Populus trichocarpa, p. 126: "slender branchlets ... marked by many orange-colored lenticels ... reddish brown during their first year, gradually becoming dark gray". Colour chosen by eye for reddish brown.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Sargent's Manual (2nd ed. 1922, read at the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18), as Populus trichocarpa, p. 126: "Leaves broad-ovate ... 3'-4' long, 2'-2½' wide; petioles slender ... 1½'-2' in length".

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Sargent's Manual (2nd ed. 1922, read at the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18), as Populus trichocarpa, p. 126: "Leaves broad-ovate ... 3'-4' long, 2'-2½' wide; petioles slender ... 1½'-2' in length".

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Sargent's Manual (2nd ed. 1922, read at the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18), as Populus trichocarpa, p. 126: "Leaves broad-ovate ... 3'-4' long, 2'-2½' wide; petioles slender ... 1½'-2' in length".

traits.shade_tolerance.note: FEIS's black cottonwood review (Populus balsamifera subsp. trichocarpa, read 2026-10-16): "Black cottonwood is very shade intolerant"; it typically has "a straight, branch-free trunk for more than half its length and a broad, open crown".

generator.params.bloom_area.note: The leaf area its `bloom` look draws on an organ 1 m long (visual forms Skill 2, 2026-10-14; plantc atlas), so it shades with what it shows: the flower now takes its family's flower plan from Simpson and Floral Diagrams (before, 0.639), and since 2026-10-16 its family's two carpels and its order's regular flowers (before, 0.031). Since 2026-10-16 its flowers, which have no perianth, are drawn by their stamens grown to the flower's size (before, 0.0138).

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.pipe_tip.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B): the twig's and the leaf's pipe radii are scaled together so the stem's diameter at breast height matches the oldest reference size; the fuller crowns of broadleaf revision 11 carry more leaf, so the yearly rings (pipe_rings) are fitted near zero and the pipe model sets the diameter. Since broadleaf revision 28 its pipe_organ and pipe_rings are the broadleaf trees' rules (0, with Leonardo's rule and dead twigs kept as heartwood); this pipe_tip stays.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: the tallest broadleaf tree of the region, with a straight stem, an open crown of upswept branches and alternate, broadly heart-shaped leaves on long stalks. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 30 m tall and 55 cm across at breast height at 40 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: dark, glossy leaves; grey bark, deeply furrowed with age. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): smooth grey-green when young, deeply furrowed and dark grey when old; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Leaf families (plant roadmap P4, `families`): sun leaves somewhat smaller and narrower than shade leaves; set from general knowledge of sun and shade leaves and juvenile foliage, not measured.

taxon.note: Common name (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

taxon.scientific_name.note: WCVP v16's accepted name for the plant the spec's authors wrote as Populus trichocarpa, which WCVP treats as a synonym.

taxon.genus.note: The genus WCVP v16's accepted name is written in.
